source_text: Verum haec omissa faciamus, et illud, quod a vobis apparet posse in hoc loco referri, rationis viribus deteramus. Si ergo dixeris, scriptum esse de hac commixtione, quod fiant duo in carne una, et secundum hunc modum, Apostolum per unum hominem [n78] dixisse, ut adhaerentia sibi generantium membra signaret; respondebo hoc quoque contra vestram impietatem valere. Non enim dictum est: Erunt duo homines in uno homine; sed: Erunt duo in carne una [n79] ; quo unitionis nomine voluptas illa coeuntium et libido, quae sensum afficiens membra consternat ac, sicut ille prudens intellexit, unam carnem gestit efficere, a Deo instituta et corporibus ante peccatum doceretur inserta.
pass_a_gloss: But let us make these things omitted, and let us wear down by the forces of reason that which appears able to be brought back by you in this place. If therefore you shall have said that it is written about this mingling that two become in one flesh, and according to this mode the Apostle said through one human being, that he might sign the members of those generating clinging to themselves; I will answer that this also avails against your impiety. For it has not been said: Two human beings will be in one human being; but: They will be two in one flesh; by which name of uniting that pleasure of those coupling and lust, which affecting the sense lays the members prostrate and, as that prudent man understood, strives to make one flesh, would be taught as instituted by God and inserted into bodies before sin.

lemmas.lexica: LS generatio; Blaise vs imitatio in Rom 5:12
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: Let us leave that aside and crush, by reason’s strength, the argument it seems you could offer at this point. You may say that Scripture describes this union by saying that the two become one flesh, and that in this sense the apostle said ‘through one man’ to indicate the joined bodies of those who beget (Romans 5:12). I will answer that this too counts against your impiety. For it does not say, ‘The two human beings will become one human being,’ but, ‘The two will become one flesh’ (Genesis 2:24). The language of union teaches that this pleasure of those coupling, this desire which affects their sensation and stirs their organs—which, as that wise man understood, strives to make one flesh—was instituted by God and implanted in their bodies before sin.

choices.why: Julian's target is Augustine's claim that sin is transmitted by begetting; keep generation vs imitation.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
